text: here is one that almost got past me and i lost it there for a bit ngl cuz it only shows on some things but this one right here. thats a classic stinker if i ever knew one. what the fuck good does saying 12 fixed slots to me in a 12 slot paged list do when it also says 1-12 lmao  [Image #10]
resolution: Removed the redundant 'N fixed slots' / 'fixed rows' page-footer flavor. The content-browser pager (LibraryPanel.tsx:111) read '1-12 / 28 - 12 fixed slots' — the '12 fixed slots' is the page size, which the '1-12' range already conveys, and there is also a '1/3' page-of-pages pill immediately beside it, so it was doubly redundant. 'fixed slots' is a layout implementation detail (the list pre-allocates a fixed number of row slots to dodge MAX_CHILDREN eviction), not user-facing information. Cut the suffix → '1-12 / 28'. Found and fixed the same leaky jargon in the File Explorer results head (FileExplorerDialog.tsx:92, '12 / 28 visible fixed rows'); since slots = files.slice(0, RESULT_SLOTS) it's an honest showing-N-of-M, so reworded to '12 of 28' and dropped 'visible fixed rows'. pageSize is still used by the paging math (no dead const); both files parse clean via esbuild transform; not shipped (live session).
